circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various supporting motorsport events. The venue holds the highest FIA classification for circuit safety and infrastructure standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a reconstruction and shortening of the track, it was rebranded and again hosted the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital positioned along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards under the management of Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and has hosted the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the Middle East's inaugural F1 race. Beyond Formula One, the venue accommodates various motorsport disciplines including GP2 racing, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, with multiple circuit configurations available and a FIA Grade 1 classification.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for teams and drivers. With FIA Grade 1 certification and spectator capacity exceeding 140,000, the venue serves as a premier racing destination in Catalonia, Spain.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7. 004 km circuit in the Walloon region of Belgium near Spa has served as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925 and participated in Formula One's inaugural season in 1950. With the exception of 2003 and 2006, the venue has hosted a round of the championship annually from 1985 onwards.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsporting competitions, including sports car racing series and North American open-wheel championships.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has served as the primary venue for China's Formula One Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. Located in China's major metropolis, the track hosts multiple motorsport events including the newly introduced Shanghai ePrix series beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone Circuit has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since hosting the inaugural race in 1948, and notably staged the first-ever World Championship round in 1950. Following decades of alternating with other venues, the Grand Prix permanently established itself at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the circuit continues to welcome international motorcycle racing as well.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One venue in Eastern Europe when it hosted its inaugural grand prix in 1986, constructed in just eight months on an accelerated timeline. Located in Mogyoród outside the capital, this 4. 381 km circuit was built following government preference for a new facility rather than a street course through Budapest's main park, marking a historic moment for motorsport behind the Iron Curtain.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit established in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The Italian Grand Prix, held there continuously since 1949 except for a 1980 closure, represents the track's premier event, making it one of only four circuits to appear on every Formula One calendar since the championship's inception.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and is operated by Honda Mobilityland. The venue holds 155,000 spectators and serves as a premier location for Formula One and Super Formula racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving around the iconic Las Vegas Boulevard with its collection of world-famous resorts and entertainment venues. The track incorporates several of the region's most recognizable landmarks, such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who perished in racing accidents in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix during three separate eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current configuration, with the event now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 turns and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track became home to the Miami Grand Prix when it joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, spanning 3. 337 km around the harbour area. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of the track traverses that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining Formula One's schedule in 2021, though this arrangement concluded in 2026. The venue, situated just inland from the North Sea, had previously been known as Circuit Park Zandvoort before undergoing a sponsorship rebrand in 2017.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated near Lusail north of Doha in Qatar, spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years prior. The venue hosts major motor racing events and incorporates additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has been home to the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021, while also hosting international electric racing events starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas in its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various racing skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the primary venue for the United States Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond its F1 commitment, the track regularly hosts major international motorsport competitions including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and various endurance racing championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 race victories over his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso holds the distinction of winning multiple endurance racing titles, including the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans 24 Hours victories, making him the sole driver to achieve success across both Formula One and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight Grand Prix victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One representing Audi, bringing his professional motorsport experience to the grid.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career. He has achieved two World Championship runner-up finishes while with Mercedes and secured ten race victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine, representing his nation on the sport's premier racing stage.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve role with Haas while primarily competing in LMP2 sports car racing with Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series. Between 2024 and 2025, he made seven Formula One race appearances.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He previously achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver racing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under France's national colours.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton holds seven Formula One World Championship titles, equalling Michael Schumacher's record, and currently races for Ferrari. His career achievements include leading records for race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes across the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, while his endurance racing achievements include a 2015 Le Mans 24 Hours victory with Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 championship standings. Since his Formula One debut, he has secured nine Grand Prix victories across nine seasons of competition.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, last competed in Formula One during 2024 after previous stints between 2014 and 2020. He has since transitioned to the FIA World Endurance Championship, where he drives for BMW through WRT, while also competing part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British Formula One driver, claimed the 2025 drivers' championship while racing for McLaren. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The veteran competitor achieved a career-defining victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that has yielded six race victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri competes for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport across four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight grand prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following prior experience in IMSA's LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, currently holds a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after completing a full-time Formula One campaign from 2021 through 2025, before transitioning to a backup position in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, having claimed four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, Verstappen has accumulated 72 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 to 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently supports the team in a developmental capacity while maintaining his connection to the sport's premier racing series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has operated under the Alpine Racing banner since 2021, initially as Renault's factory outfit before the French manufacturer's withdrawal concluded at the end of 2025. Previously known as Renault F1 Team, the outfit adopted the Alpine marque to highlight the luxury sports car division within Groupe Renault's portfolio. The team maintained its works status throughout this period until Renault's departure from the championship.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has entered Formula One racing through multiple organisational structures, with its current iteration competing as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished outfit, participating in every world championship since the series' 1950 inception. The team, nicknamed after its distinctive emblem, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's history while accumulating the most championship success of any competitor.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American Formula One team in 2014, launching its competitive program in 2016. Under the leadership of Ayao Komatsu, who took over as team principal in 2024 following Guenther Steiner's departure, the squad continues to compete in the sport.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm built sports cars and Formula One chassis, winning two endurance world championships and the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours before joining Formula One in 1993. The team underwent numerous transformations during its 32-year Grand Prix tenure, becoming the sport's fourth-longest-serving constructor before being acquired by Audi in 2024 to establish their factory racing operation.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing competes in Formula One as a British outfit headquartered at its facility in Woking. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group corporate structure, which is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team based in Brackley and holding a German racing licence. Known colloquially as the "Silver Arrows," the squad operates as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team and has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff since January 2022.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing, it operates as a sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as Red Bull's secondary team alongside the flagship Red Bull Racing operation.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from an English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has become one of two teams controlled by the Red Bull conglomerate. The squad was led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade existence before Laurent Mekies assumed the team principal role in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and operates from a substantial facility in the English Midlands.
